title: Cell-attached capacitance measurements at release sites of a central nerve terminal
protocol: Prepare parasigittal brainstem slices 200 μm thick from 6-8 days old Wistar rats using a vibratome.
Position brain slices in the recording chamber.
Select a large calyx approximately 1-2 μm in thickness on the surface of the slice.
Use a large pipette 1-2 MΩ to form a loose patch on the postsynaptic membrane.
Suck the postsynaptic neuronal cell body into the pipette by applying strong suction to the pipette.
Pull away the pipette, exposing the calyx membrane that was originally opposing the postsynaptic neuron.
Use a polished pipette 4-6 MΩ heavily coated with sylgard near the tip to form a cell-attached patch at the exposed presynaptic membrane.
After forming a high resistance (>10 GΩ) seal, stop the perfusion system.
Lower the bath solution level to just above the slice, which helps to reduce noise.
Make cell-attached capacitance measurements with an SR830 2-phase lock-in amplifier coupled to an EPC-8 patch-clamp amplifier.
Superimpose a 20 KHz sine wave (rms: 200 mV) on a command potential of 0 mV.
Low-pass filter the in-phase and out-of-phase current outputs at 0.1-1 ms (24 dB).
Digitize the filtered signals at 16 bits.
Read the digitized signals into a Macintosh computer.
Set the gain of an EPC-8 amplifier to 50 mV/pA.
Adjust C<sub>slow</sub> and G<sub>slow</sub> to 0.2 pF and 0.2 μS, respectively.
Minimize the sinusoidal current by adjusting C<sub>fast</sub> and G<sub>fast</sub>.
Connect the current output of the EPC-8 amplifier to the lock-in amplifier input through a 10:1 voltage divider.
Adjust the initial phase setting of the lock-in amplifier to null changes in Re trace induced by dithering a 100-fF calibration installed in the capacitance compensation circuit.
Apply gentle suction of the membrane via the pipette every 100-200 seconds during each patch of cell-attached recordings.
Use the transient capacitance increase caused by the gentle suction to correct phase errors offline.
After the experiment, re-compute Re and Im traces with the phase shift varied in 2° increments until the projection in the Re trace during a gentle suction is eliminated.
Adjust the phase correction to eliminate the visible persistent change in Re trace associated with non-flicker up-steps in the Im trace of the same patch.
Occasionally observe flickers in Re trace without accompanying changes in Im trace, which might reflect openings and closings of a single ion channel.
